ledger.note: 17 December 1803: Raghoji II signs the Treaty of Deogaon and gives up Cuttack. "On 17 December 1803, Raghoji II Bhonsale of Nagpur signed the Treaty of Deogaon" after Argaon (29 November 1803), giving up "the province of Cuttack" with Balasore and parts of Midnapore; the Nagpur page adds southern Berar and Sambalpur. The reading of "southern Berar" as the two circles is mine.
1806: Sambalpur passes to the British. Ceded at Deogaon but "Sambalpur was not relinquished until 1806".

notes: Six pages opened (Kingdom of Nagpur, Raghoji I Bhonsle, Maratha invasions of Bengal, Treaty of Deogaon, Second and Third Anglo-Maratha War). Founding: 1739 (infobox) against 1743 (text); the infobox status line runs 1729-1818. The pages do not date Berar, Chhattisgarh, Chanda or Sambalpur beyond the span 1745-1755, nor give the Bhonsle holdings between 1818 and 1853 (Chhattisgarh and Chanda are kept in the remnant by reading); shapes are circles around the provincial towns and total about 175,000-185,000 km2 against 217,560 km2 on the infobox (no year). Appa Sahib's deposition and Raghuji III's installation are not drawn. The kingdom lies inside the maratha-empire Cliopatria shape until 1818. Counterparts needing dossiers: gond-kingdom-of-deogarh (and the Chanda Gond kingdom, Raipur/Ratanpur Haihayas, Sambalpur) and nawabs-of-bengal (Cliopatria row, other group). british-empire (sa-06) should record a vassal_start for kingdom-of-nagpur from 1818 to 1853.
